summary:
EASD 2026 (Milan) is the main source of signals this week. The two biggest openings are the duelling company claims, because each one names a drug people already search for: Lilly says Zepbound beat Wegovy HD in an indirect comparison, and Novo says staying on Ozempic 2 mg beat switching to Mounjaro in a real-world study. Both claims fall apart once you look at how they were measured. In Lilly's comparison, the gap mostly disappears in the 'if people stayed on treatment' analysis (1.8% and 0.7%, not significant). In Novo's study, the difference is a 6% relative difference (HR 1.06) and it's observational. These fit our best-performing title format, the headline decoder that names a drug.

The best early-stage opportunities with real substance:
- trevogrumab with semaglutide halved lean mass loss in the Phase 2 COURAGE trial (6.7% vs 3.3% at 26 weeks; in press at The Lancet)
- the orforglipron (Foundayo) pill passed its heart-safety test against insulin glargine in the ACHIEVE-4 trial (Lancet; HR 0.84)
- survodutide reached up to 13.1% weight loss vs 3.1% on placebo in SYNCHRONIZE-2 (NEJM)
- in a real-world study (OCTANE), people who switched from injections to the Wegovy pill lost 4.1% (n=194, Ro telehealth data, no control group)

Retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2 (Lancet) is at its peak. The search terms are moving to 'is retatrutide FDA approved?', which we can answer with a dated status. The 'metabolic whiplash' topic is still being picked up by mainstream outlets. The nail and hair study (39% vs 9%) got wide mainstream coverage today, but we already posted a Short on it on 10-01, so only a deeper long-form is worth doing.

Lower-priority but credible: semaglutide and liver fat (post hoc, only 26 people), postpartum GLP-1 prescriptions up 24-fold (JAMA), petrelintide, safiglipron, and Novo's $675 list price from Jan 2027. I rejected microdosing because it breaks our guardrails. Topics already covered in earlier snapshots (SELECT mediation, pancreatic cancer) were left out unless they had a new hook.

Sources: [HCPLive nails](https://www.hcplive.com/view/nail-detachment-4-times-more-common-with-glp-1-use), [News-Medical trevogrumab](https://www.news-medical.net/news/20261001/Trevogrumab-cuts-semaglutide-induced-lean-mass-loss-by-half-study-shows.aspx), [GlobeNewswire Wegovy liver](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/01/3372708/0/en/novo-s-wegovy-semaglutide-reduced-liver-fat-to-normal-levels-in-9-out-of-10-adults-with-obesity-and-excess-liver-fat-easd2026.html), [CBS price cut](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/wegovy-ozempic-novo-nordisk-price-cut-january-2027/), [HCPLive COMPETE SWITCH](https://www.hcplive.com/view/semaglutide-2-mg-escalation-tied-to-lower-mace-vs-tirzepatide-switch-in-t2d), [HCPLive ACHIEVE-4](https://www.hcplive.com/view/achieve-4-orforglipron-non-inferior-to-insulin-glargine-for-cardiovascular-protection-in-t2d), [Pharmacy Times ITC](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/tirzepatide-linked-to-more-weight-loss-than-semaglutide-7-2-mg), [BioPharm OCTANE](https://www.biopharminternational.com/view/wegovy-pill-delivers-4-1-weight-loss-in-patients-switching-from-injectables-real-world-octane-data-show), [USC Schaeffer postpartum](https://schaeffer.usc.edu/research/glp-1-prescriptions-for-new-mothers-have-increased-sharply/), [GlobeNewswire survodutide](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/01/3372564/0/en/boehringer-ingelheim-s-survodutide-achieves-up-to-13-1-weight-loss-in-new-phase-iii-trial-alongside-significant-improvements-in-glycemic-control-in-people-with-obesity-and-type-2-d.html)

candidates.topic: Did tirzepatide (Zepbound) really beat semaglutide 7.2 mg (Wegovy HD)? Lilly's EASD indirect comparison of SURMOUNT-1 vs STEP UP
candidates.angle: Headline decoder. Lilly's headline number (+4.5% more loss for tirzepatide 15 mg, +3.2% for 10 mg) comes from the 'everyone randomised' (treatment-regimen) analysis. In the 'if they stayed on treatment' (efficacy) analysis the gap shrinks to 1.8% and 0.7% and is no longer statistically significant. This was a Lilly-funded comparison of two separate 72-week trials in adults without diabetes, not a head-to-head trial. Point to SURMOUNT-5 as the real head-to-head trial, which tested tirzepatide against semaglutide 2.4 mg, not 7.2 mg. Message: both work well, so talk to your prescriber.
keywords: which is stronger zepbound or wegovy
candidates.why_now: The Lilly release went out on 29 Sep and Pharmacy Times covered it on 1 Oct. The Wegovy HD (7.2 mg) dose is new, so people are searching 'Wegovy HD vs Zepbound'. This matches our best title formulas: headline decoder plus named drug.

evidence.signal: Treatment-regimen estimand +4.5% / +3.2%; efficacy estimand 1.8% / 0.7%, not significant; Lilly-funded indirect comparison
Company claim: tirzepatide 10/15 mg associated with more weight loss than semaglutide 7.2 mg
Separate indirect comparison of tirzepatide vs semaglutide in adults without T2D (28 Sep)

candidates.topic: Novo says staying on Ozempic 2 mg beat switching to Mounjaro for heart events: COMPETE SWITCH CV, real-world, 636,525 adults with type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: Headline decoder. Novo's '6% lower risk' comes from a hazard ratio of 1.06 (95% CI 1.04–1.08) in a Novo-run retrospective analysis. It's an association with possible residual confounding, and safety wasn't assessed. Explain what a 6% relative difference means, and be clear that it's not a reason to switch or stop anything yourself. Ideal follow-up to the Lilly decoder: 'Novo vs Lilly: two EASD claims, decoded'.
keywords: should I switch from ozempic to mounjaro
ozempic mounjaro heart attack stroke study
candidates.why_now: Novo's release went out on 29 Sep and HCPLive, Pharmacy Times and Cardiovascular Business picked it up through 1 Oct. Searching 'should I switch' is a common real-life question. Few creators have explained the HR 1.06 nuance yet.

evidence.signal: Adjusted HR 1.06 (1.04–1.08), 636,525 adults with T2D; escalation to semaglutide 2 mg vs switch to tirzepatide
Company states residual confounding can't be excluded; safety not assessed
Framed as Novo and Lilly pitting their GLP-1s against each other at EASD

candidates.topic: Trevogrumab plus semaglutide halved lean mass loss: Phase 2 COURAGE trial (EASD 2026, in press at The Lancet)
candidates.angle: 'Can a second drug protect your muscle on semaglutide?' At 26 weeks, lean mass loss was 6.7% on semaglutide alone vs 3.3% with trevogrumab 75 mg. In the MRI substudy, about 70% of muscle loss was prevented. Make clear it's experimental, Phase 2 and not approved. Then turn it into what helps today: protein (with the kidney caveat) and strength training. Never point to 'research peptide' sellers.
candidates.why_now: Reuters, News-Medical, Medical Xpress and Endpoints covered it between 30 Sep and 1 Oct. Muscle loss is one of the biggest GLP-1 worries, and creator coverage of the trevogrumab name is still thin. Our playbook lists muscle as a topic to double down on.

evidence.signal: Lean mass loss cut by ~50% vs semaglutide plus placebo; MRI substudy ~70% of muscle loss prevented
Phase 2 COURAGE results presented at EASD
Trial registration

candidates.topic: Is the orforglipron (Foundayo) pill safe for the heart? ACHIEVE-4 vs insulin glargine in 2,749 adults with type 2 diabetes at higher heart risk (Lancet)
candidates.angle: Named-drug question: 'Is Foundayo safe for your heart?' Major heart events were non-inferior to insulin glargine (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20). Weight fell 8.8%, a difference of about 10.4 points vs glargine. The lower all-cause death rate (HR 0.43) was a secondary result with a nominal p-value, so treat it with caution, and give absolute rates in the script. The trial was open-label, and 'safe vs insulin' is not the same as 'proven to protect the heart'.
candidates.why_now: Published in The Lancet on 30 Sep, with coverage from Medscape, Healio and HCPLive on 1 Oct. Foundayo is a newly approved pill that people search by name, and it has some momentum with us already (the orforglipron long-form was our top long-form).

evidence.signal: Phase 3, event-driven, open-label, non-inferiority trial vs insulin glargine
MACE HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20); all-cause mortality HR 0.43 nominal; −8.8% weight
Company framing: CV safety in largest, longest T2D study

candidates.topic: Switching from GLP-1 injections to the Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide): 4.1% further weight loss at 3 months in real-world OCTANE data
candidates.angle: 'Does the Wegovy pill work as well as the shot?' People in this study kept losing weight after switching (an average of 4.1%, or 4.0 kg, in 3 months). Give the limits: 194 adults on one telehealth platform (Ro), no control group, presented by Novo, only 3 months of follow-up. Explain why pills need different habits (taking them with water on an empty stomach, as directed). Any switch is a decision for your prescriber.
keywords: switching from ozempic to wegovy pill
candidates.why_now: CNBC and Reuters covered it on 30 Sep and Yahoo Finance on 1 Oct. 'Does the semaglutide pill work' is already showing up as a search term in the feeds. Pills vs injections is a hot consumer question.

evidence.signal: OCTANE: 194 switchers, 4.1% weight loss at 3 months, Ro telehealth retrospective data
Mainstream pickup

candidates.topic: Is retatrutide FDA approved? TRIUMPH-2 in The Lancet (up to 20.8% vs 4.0% placebo at 80 weeks, adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes): status as of Oct 2026
candidates.angle: An attributed correction plus a status explainer, built on our 'Lilly says online retatrutide isn't its trial drug' winner. Cover what the Lancet paper shows (population, arms, side effects) and the fact that, as of Oct 2026, retatrutide is still investigational and available only in trials. Anything sold online isn't the trial drug. Never name or point to any source.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet paper came out on 29 Sep, with NBC, USA Today, The Guardian and Scientific American all covering it. Search-query pages for 'retatrutide approval status' and 'fda concerns unapproved retatrutide' are appearing. Coverage is at its peak, so only the approval-status and safety angle stands out.

evidence.signal: Phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trial in obesity plus T2D
Momentum 86→92 across 2 snapshots

candidates.topic: Survodutide in SYNCHRONIZE-2 (NEJM): up to 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo weight loss at 76 weeks in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: 'The GLP-1/glucagon drug you haven't heard of.' Explain the glucagon mechanism and the liver-fat angle. Use the efficacy estimand label and placebo next to every number: A1C down up to 1.21% vs 0.03%, and ≥5% weight loss in up to 79.3% vs 32.7%. Add date-hedged status: investigational as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD and published in NEJM on 1 Oct, but covered only by trade press (HCPLive, BioSpace). Almost no creator coverage. It's a named next-gen drug, which our data says performs.

evidence.signal: Up to 13.1% vs 3.1% at 76 weeks, efficacy estimand; NEJM
SYNCHRONIZE-2 outperforms placebo on weight and blood sugar

candidates.topic: 'Ozempic nails': first controlled study finds nail detachment in 39% of GLP-1 users vs 9% of controls (EADV 2026), plus hair-loss figures
candidates.angle: Long-form deep dive, since we already posted a Short on 10-01. Cover the numbers (nail detachment 39% vs 9%; unusual hair loss 50% vs 34%), and that the gap shrank to about 2–3× after adjustment. It was self-reported and about half of users had nail problems before treatment. Weight loss alone didn't explain it. Controls had T2D or obesity, but don't apply that to everyone. Finish with gentle, evidence-based habits (protein and nutrient adequacy, seeing a dermatologist).
candidates.why_now: US News, HealthDay, Medical Economics and HCPLive all covered it on 1 Oct. Side effects people search for are a double-down topic for us.

evidence.signal: 39% vs 9% nail detachment; 575 users vs 1,329 controls
First controlled study; adjusted associations still about 2–3×
Mainstream pickup on 1 Oct

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) vs tirzepatide 15 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity (Phase 2, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'What is EloraTZP, and why does adding amylin matter?' Explain amylin simply, give Lilly's reported numbers with the comparator, and note that MarketWatch reported more side effects with the combination. Status: Phase 2, investigational as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: Covered by Reuters, CNBC, WSJ, STAT and Fierce between 30 Sep and 1 Oct. Momentum in our snapshots is 90→88. It's an amylin wave (petrelintide and CagriSema too), and our CagriSema Short did well.

evidence.signal: EloraTZP beat tirzepatide on weight loss and A1C in T2D
More weight loss, but more side effects

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1s and heart risk ('metabolic whiplash'): 333,000 US veterans with type 2 diabetes, up to 22% higher risk after 2 years off
candidates.angle: Positive, practical framing: why benefits may depend on staying on treatment, what the study can and can't show (observational, veterans with T2D), and what to discuss with a prescriber about cost or side effects before any gap. Never advise on stopping. Tie it to the new cost-and-adherence study (UGA).
keywords: what happens when you stop glp-1
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 of our snapshots (momentum 84→74) and still being picked up: Scripps News and Yahoo creators on 1 Oct. UGA's 'higher costs, lower adherence' adds a fresh hook.

evidence.signal: Mainstream pickup on 1 Oct
Higher GLP-1 costs linked to lower adherence

candidates.topic: Semaglutide (Wegovy) and fatty liver: 23 of 26 adults with excess liver fat reached normal levels at 72 weeks (STEP UP post hoc, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Benefits beyond weight, with a named drug and honest scale. Average liver fat fell from 8.8% to 3.1% in the 55-person MRI subgroup. Only 26 people started above 5%, the analysis was post hoc, and liver fat wasn't a pre-specified endpoint. Connect it to the stronger MASH evidence (ESSENCE trial) and keep the claim strength low.
candidates.why_now: Novo's release went out on 1 Oct and Benzinga and Yahoo picked it up. Fatty liver is a high-search topic that creators rarely cover with proper caveats.

evidence.signal: 88.5% of those with liver fat >5% reached <5% at week 72
8.8% → 3.1% in 55-adult subgroup

candidates.topic: New GLP-1 prescriptions after childbirth up 24-fold (JAMA, about 1 million births), plus a French nationwide study on GLP-1 safety in pregnancy (Diabetologia)
candidates.angle: 'GLP-1s after pregnancy: what we know and don't.' New prescriptions rose from 0.08% to 1.9% of new mothers, and to about 1 in 6 of those with T2D. Experts say breastfeeding data is limited. The pregnancy studies are reassuring but observational. Message: plan with your clinician, especially if breastfeeding or planning another pregnancy.
candidates.why_now: The JAMA paper and USC release came out on 1 Oct, with Medical Xpress and Yahoo the same evening. That's very early. Pregnancy-outcome reviews appeared the same day.

evidence.signal: 0.08% → 1.9% of new mothers starting GLP-1 within 6 months (JAMA)
French nationwide study on GLP-1 safety in pregnancy with T2D

candidates.topic: Ozempic and Wegovy US list price drops to $675 on 1 Jan 2027: what it means for people who pay through deductibles or co-insurance
candidates.angle: A practical explainer: a list-price cut matters most for people with high deductibles or co-insurance, while people with fixed copays may see little change. Date-hedge it ('announced Feb 2026, effective Jan 2027'). Point people to their insurer or prescriber, never to compounded or gray-market sources.
candidates.predicted_peak: Nov–Jan (open enrollment and new plan year)
candidates.why_now: Medical Economics resurfaced it on 1 Oct, and US open enrollment starts this month. The Medicare GLP-1 program is also back in the news (The Hill).

evidence.signal: Wegovy −50%, Ozempic −35% to $675 from 1 Jan 2027

candidates.topic: Petrelintide, an amylin analogue on its own: ZUPREME-1 Phase 2 (Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology)
candidates.angle: Name the drug: 'Petrelintide: the amylin shot that could be gentler on the stomach?' Only make the tolerability claim if the paper supports it. Compare the mechanism with GLP-1 and fit it into the amylin wave alongside CagriSema and EloraTZP. Investigational as of Oct 2026.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet D&E paper came out on 29 Sep, alongside an amylin review in Diabetes Ther. Mainstream coverage is minimal so far.

evidence.signal: ZUPREME 1 randomised, placebo-controlled Phase 2
Review of new amylin-based agonists

candidates.topic: Safiglipron, a new oral small-molecule GLP-1 pill, in early type 2 diabetes (Nature Medicine RCT)
candidates.angle: 'Another GLP-1 pill is coming: what's different about small-molecule pills like orforglipron and safiglipron?' Explain why no food or water timing rules may be needed for small molecules, if the papers support it. Early-stage data with date hedging.
candidates.why_now: Published in Nature Medicine on 29 Sep with almost no consumer coverage. Pills are one of our pillars.

evidence.signal: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in early T2D

candidates.topic: Creatine for muscle loss on GLP-1 medicines (Clinical Nutrition commentary) alongside STEP UP thigh-muscle MRI data
candidates.angle: Evergreen muscle-pillar refresh tied to the trevogrumab news. What protein and strength training are shown to do, and why creatine is a plausible but unproven idea in GLP-1 users specifically. Kidney caveat and 'ask your clinician'. No supplement doses.
candidates.predicted_peak: Ongoing; boost now while trevogrumab news is live
candidates.why_now: The Clin Nutr commentary (21 Sep) plus COURAGE muscle news makes 'how do I keep muscle?' a timely search.

evidence.signal: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss (commentary)

candidates.angle: Not to be covered. Our brand rules ban microdosing and self-titration protocols. At most, a general line that dose decisions belong to the prescriber could appear inside other content.
candidates.why_now: Still circulating in creator media, but it falls outside our guardrails.

evidence.signal: Microdosing GLP-1s explainer on 1 Oct
